newsitem.title: UK: S&P revises Granada outlook to negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises Granada outlook to negative.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had affirmed Granada Group PLC's A minus senior rating and revised the outlook to negative from stable.

"The outlook revision reflects Standard & Poor's concerns over the cumulative effect of a slower-than-anticipated disposal programme, ongoing investment activities, and opportunistic acquisitions on the company's credit measures, which are already weak for the rating category," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said the ratings could be lowered if material debt reduction did not occur within the next 12-18 months.

"The ratings reflect Granada's leading U.K. market positions in four business areas: media, restaurants, hotels and rentals, and Standard & Poor's expectation that planned asset sales will further strengthen the company's financial profile, which benefits from a solid track record of profit growth and free cash flow generation," the agency said.

It said the ratings also incorporated the business benefits, such as diversification and synergies, of Granada's acquisition of Forte plc in early 1996, offset by the sizable acquisition price of 5.4 billion stg (including assumed debt).

S&P said while Granada had financial flexibility in terms of potential asset sale candidates, significant debt reduction was needed to bring Granada's credit measures more in line with a A minus rating.
"Maintenance of the current rating over the medium term assumes recovery in credit measures, including pretax net fixed charge cover reaching a minimum of 4 times," S&P said.
It said if an improvement in credit measures was absent, the ratings could be lowered.

"Ratings do not currently incorporate the possibility of further restructurings, such as demerging certain of the group's main business interests, which could have uncertain implications for credit quality," Standard & Poor's said.
